THE SCHOOL: A MAGAZINE DEVOTED TO ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION
Volume 1 (Toronto: University of Toronto / Ontario College of Education, 1912-13)
Internet Archive: schoolmagazinede01univuoft

NOT LENDING-RESTRICTED. The complete djvu text was downloaded (1,671,490 bytes) and searched.
"Kanawana" occurs ZERO times in this volume. What it carries is F. H. SPINNEY, who this project
knows only as Kamp Kanawana's EDUCATIONAL DIRECTOR, documented in his fifth year in the 1921
brochure and teaching basketry in 1922, with no biography of any kind.

He was a Montreal public-school principal and a published writer on pedagogy, five years earlier.

The extracts below are quoted from the scan's own text. Its double-spacing has been collapsed;
nothing else is altered, and the OCR's own slips ("F, H.", "K. H.", "G. A. Comish") are left where
they fall.

Archbishop — (after putting the crown upon Arthur's head).
"Thou art king of England." (Turning to the knights and
barons present), "I present thee with King Arthur, men of
England." (All shout.)


In the Little Red Schoolhouse

F. H. SPINNEY
Principal Alexandra School, Montreal.

(One of a series of articles pertaining to the work of the rural school.)

I

MISS BROWN, the teacher in the little red school,
certainly gave a uide berth to any path of routine
that could be designated as a "rut".


--- The by-line, eighth instalment (scan line 35168) ---



In the Little Red Schoolhouse

F. H. SPINNEY,

Principal, Alexandra Public School, Montreal.

(A series of articles relating to the work of the rural school — yet sug-
gestive for all teachers. Have you read the previous numbers?)

VIII. General Equipment.

IN the last issue we observed the "study period", just pre-
ceding the noon dismissal, and the departure of the
pupils, one by one, as each gave proof of a thorough
preparation of the assignment for that period. The children's
delight in getting out early arose, not from a dislike for school,
but rather from a consciousness of having made their very
best efforts, and perhaps more from winning the teacher's
approving smile. The approving smile of a popular teacher,


--- The magazine announces a second series from him (scan line 37140) ---



THE SCHOOL


learn that Mr. Spinney will contribute a second series of
articles, entitled "Little Journeys to Rural Schools". We
shall also have a number of short articles on Primary Language
Work, The Equipment of a Science Room, The Twentieth
Century Inspector, Waste Effort in Teaching. Arrangements
are being made for other articles, and fuller announcement
will be made in our September number.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED
-------------------
F. H. Spinney was PRINCIPAL OF ALEXANDRA SCHOOL (later given as ALEXANDRA PUBLIC SCHOOL),
MONTREAL, and contributed a serial column, "IN THE LITTLE RED SCHOOLHOUSE", to volume 1 of The
School — at least EIGHT numbered instalments, I through VIII, on the practice of the rural
one-room school, described by the magazine as "suggestive for all teachers". The editors then
announced a SECOND SERIES from him, "Little Journeys to Rural Schools". His fellow contributors in
the same volume are the Ontario College of Education's own people — H. T. J. Coleman, W. E.
Macpherson, G. A. Cornish, F. E. Coombs — so this is a national professional journal, not a local
bulletin.

THE IDENTIFICATION, AND ITS GROUNDS. This project's F. H. Spinney is Kamp Kanawana's Educational
Director, documented in his fifth year in the 1921 brochure and teaching basketry in 1922, with no
first name, no dates and no biography. The identification with the Montreal principal rests on:
the same uncommon surname with the same two initials; the same city; the same profession; and the
exact fit of the role — a boys' camp's EDUCATIONAL Director being a schoolmaster, and this one a
schoolmaster who wrote a national column on how to teach. It is an identification by name, place
and calling, and it is written that way rather than asserted.

A NEAR MISS WORTH RECORDING. Three Harvard College Observatory annual reports (report1913harv,
report1914harv, report1915harv, report1916harv) list a "Mr. F. H. Spinney" among their volunteer
variable-star observers, and one of them gives his residence: HUDSON, N.H. That is a different
man, and a query on the name alone returns him four times out of twelve. The Alberta "Alexandra
School" that appears in this same volume's news column is in MEDICINE HAT and is likewise not his.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: his first name, his dates, when he came to or left Kanawana beyond the
1917-1922 the brochures imply, and whether the second series was ever written. LATER VOLUMES OF
THE SCHOOL, which ran to 1935 and are on the Internet Archive, are UNSEARCHED — and the run covers
every year of his known Kanawana service.
